# Performance verdict: PR #257

**BLOCK** at `d968afe002b745c8f43eac5a6d80783bf8b88601`.
Request: `01a1f247-a946-7440-b5b0-2b454ec68f7f`.

## Blocking finding

**P257-1 — HIGH: the newly niced canonical test recipe conflicts with an existing macOS scheduling assertion.**

`justfile:117-118` now runs every Vitest worker under `/usr/bin/nice -n 19`. `harness/scripts/shared-build.test.ts:104-137` inherits the worker's scheduling when it starts shared-build; `harness/scripts/shared-build.sh:341-351` applies another `nice -n 19`. The unchanged assertion at `shared-build.test.ts:306-309` requires literal `niceness=19` for all three children. On this Mac the composed adjustment produces 20, not 19.

Direct process-priority receipts, without running any tests or builds:

```sh
/usr/bin/nice -n 19 /bin/sh -c 'exec /bin/ps -o ni= -p $$'
# 19
/usr/bin/nice -n 19 /usr/bin/nice -n 19 /bin/sh -c 'exec /bin/ps -o ni= -p $$'
# 20
```

This exact inherited-priority failure was already observed in `docs/retros/pij-previous-firefly-plan-227.md:3-6`. The new recipe makes it the normal `just test` / `harness checks` path rather than an externally niced invocation. **Inference from the executed priority probe plus current source:** that existing assertion fails through the new canonical path. I did not rerun it under the no-local-tests instruction.

The green CI check does not exercise this composition: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:68` invokes bare `npm test`, on Linux. Its log shows `shared-build.test.ts` passing under that different invocation.

Smallest correction: retain test-runner nice; remove the brittle exact-19 snapshot and validate the actual safety invariant under inherited priority (cargo must not run at higher scheduling priority than the required safe level). Have the implementation owner provide proof through the canonical niced entry point; do not make a local gate green by dropping the priority protection.

## Cost assessment

The target and nested-build cutover is directionally sound. It adds no daemon timer, poll, hook, status-line or launch site; the Rust daemon and `spawn_sites.rs` are unchanged. Existing shared-build waiting is reached by more recipes, so its per-waiter cost matters.

| Changed path | Cost and scaling | Evidence / limit |
|---|---|---|
| Default target selection | Two git invocations per helper call, no background work; one target per Git common directory | `cargo-target.sh:16-25`; the review worktree resolves to the parent of its clone's `.git` plus `/target`. Another clone keeps its own target. Explicit environment targets still override. |
| Missing-binary Vitest fixture | No nested cargo invocation; one private binary copy when exercised | Fixture build branch removed. CI exercises watchdog smoke. Current review worktree has no `target/`; this alone is not an after-test receipt. |
| Shared-build contention | One build batch at a time per physical target. Each waiting caller polls every 20 s: one `/bin/df`, `/bin/mkdir`, `/bin/sleep` per normal tick = 0.15 external utility launches/s/waiter, plus shell subprocess work. No cost at rest. | Existing `shared-build.sh:49-59,258-321`. Lock is not FIFO; latency includes preceding builds and up to one poll interval after release; repeated acquisitions can extend it. No measured queue latency supplied. |
| Forced freshness | Touches all workspace crate entry sources once per acquired recipe; disables incremental; rust-check holds one lock for clippy then test | `shared-build.sh:333-367`; more recipes now incur this work. PR receipts: route inventory 49 s; smoke 79 s total, approximately 40 s build. These are author measurements, not repeated here. |
| Niced test runners | One nice exec per invocation; descendants inherit priority. Existing Vitest maxWorkers=4 locally remains unchanged. | `justfile`, `vitest.config.ts:47-57`. Nice lowers priority, not concurrency or runnable-process count: it cannot by itself guarantee the absence of a load-average spike. Wall time under load can increase. |
| Cargo tripwire | Shell wrapper per intercepted cargo invocation; helper path resolution executes shell/dirname work; non-build pass-through also scans PATH. No recurring work. | `harness/test-tripwire/cargo`; `metadata`, `fmt`, `--version` remain pass-through. CI's refusal and version tests pass. Wrapper is a developer guard, not a sandbox against absolute cargo paths or caller-replaced PATH. |
| Private binary copy | Approximately 142.5 MiB copied per fixture from the currently built debug binary; removed with fixture teardown | Current artifact is 149,378,712 bytes. This is not a new 2.4 GB target per lane. Physical copy allocation was not measured. |

Author before/after receipts in the PR body: one missing-binary test run on main created 2.4 GB in 69 s with one nested build; the changed fresh-worktree test run created no target, and explicit recipe runs used the shared target. Full workspace targets were reported around 15 GB per lane. Do not add the fixture's 2.4 GB to a full target's 15 GB as though these were disjoint directories: both occupy the same `target/debug` tree. Existing lane targets are not deleted by this PR.

Independent live disk observation: clone's current `target/debug` is **14G** by `du -sh`; author reported 15G earlier, so exact size is workload/time-dependent. Review worktree `du -sh target` exits 1 with no such directory. No build was performed to manufacture an after state.

## Live baseline (not a causal before/after comparison)

Measured while the fleet was running other work; no reviewed code deployed.

| Measurement | Observed value |
|---|---|
| `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json` | 20.0 s, 163.8 new processes/s machine-wide |
| Attributed lower bounds | bash 31.6/s; node 7.6/s; rustc 6.2/s; cargo 1.1/s; no daemon children observed |
| Daemon ping pair | PID unchanged; total 1531 -> 1531 over 21.752 s, 0.0000 daemon spawns/s; every per-operation counter unchanged |
| Counter window | 2026-11-19T05:29:58.019760Z -> 05:30:19.774112Z |
| Daemon resource snapshot | PID 36530; ps %CPU 15.9; RSS 146592 KiB (~143.2 MiB); elapsed 21:48 |
| Load averages, earlier -> later snapshot | 28.90 / 26.55 / 42.22 -> 20.56 / 24.80 / 40.60 |

The PID-rate probe's parent attribution is a lower bound. Daemon `ps %CPU` is the command's reported statistic, not a paired interval CPU measurement. Concurrent fleet workload prevents attributing these values or the load decrease to this unmerged harness patch.

## Verification and proof boundary

Read exact-head diff, changed cost paths, unchanged lock/nice implementation, CI workflow and historical scheduling receipt. Verified review worktree HEAD equals the full subject SHA.

Consumed actual CI job log: https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/44464878980/job/135360150200 . It shows a pre-test cargo build (38.06 s), `PIJ_RS_BIN_REQUIRED=1`, watchdog smoke 9/9, tripwire 4/4, recipe cost 8/8, shared-build 19/19, and 105 files / 2321 tests passing in 61.97 s. CI protects missing-binary coverage, but bypasses `just test` and therefore does not close P257-1.

No local tests, builds, harness boot or harness checks ran, per review instruction. Only read-only inspection, process-priority facts, disk/resource observations and requested live launch measurements ran. Build-time/disk before-after values above are explicitly the author's receipts; no controlled live-fleet before/after PR measurement exists here.

## Handoff

Fix P257-1 without removing nice, then obtain a fresh exact-head verdict. Highest-leverage harness improvement: run the canonical niced test entry point in CI, or otherwise exercise inherited scheduling, so a green bare `npm test` cannot certify a broken `just test` path. Queue latency, nice-under-load slowdown and any fleet-wide throughput improvement remain unmeasured rather than claimed.
